evals.prompt: /triage-pr-feedback 120. The PR has 4 unresolved threads: two from a human reviewer and two from CodeRabbit. One CodeRabbit thread claims a function is called with a stale token, but the caller reads the token from the store at failure time.
evals.expected_output: A numbered table with one row per thread, a verdict and evidence for each, then one question about what to apply. No files change and nothing is posted.
expectations: Fetches unresolved threads, top-level comments and review bodies before judging.
Reads the code at every location the threads name.
Marks the stale-token claim with the caller line that refutes or confirms it.
Shows one table with #, author, level, where, comment, applies?, why.
Ends with a question; makes no edit, commit, reply, or thread resolution.

evals.prompt: revisa los comentarios del PR y dime cuáles aplican. A reviewer says express wallets are charged while the card is selected, so a refusal marks the card form. In the code, the wallet form only renders when the wallet option is selected.
evals.expected_output: The wallet finding is marked as not applying, citing the component that renders the wallet only when selected. The table and question are in Spanish.
expectations: Checks where the wallet button renders before accepting the scenario.
Marks the item ❌ with the file and line that refutes the premise.
Writes the table headers and the closing question in Spanish.

evals.prompt: /triage-pr-feedback. CodeRabbit left two comments outside the diff in its latest review body, and a fourth-round comment on the same fallback function asks to copy one more selector rule into it; when the function cannot confirm a method it already shows the generic error.
evals.expected_output: Both outside-diff comments appear in the table. The fourth-round item is recommended for declining because it already fails safe, with a note that the rounds on that block are not converging.
expectations: Reads review bodies and includes outside-diff comments as rows.
Names the failure direction of the fourth-round item as a safe fallback.
Recommends declining it or moving the logic to its owner as a follow-up, instead of another patch.

evals.prompt: /triage-pr-feedback 88. A reviewer says the Yuno concrete method can stay selected from a stale session after a minimum-amount refusal. Whether that can happen depends on how the backend PR matches the minimum to the payment engine.
evals.expected_output: The row cites the backend code that decides the match, or is marked 🔎 with what was checked and what would settle it.
expectations: Reads the backend contract (the open PR or deployed branch) instead of assuming it.
Names the file and method that decide the verdict.
Uses 🔎 only when the contract cannot be confirmed, saying what would settle it.
